meta.scene_summary: We're busy building autonomous missiles and sentient traffic while our fridges can't even hold a firmware update.

cooking.headline: GPT-6 can now drive, because your commute wasn't stressful enough already
cooking.summary: OpenAI is teaching their model to handle a steering wheel, which is a bold move considering it still hallucinates basic facts about history. I can't wait for the first 'sorry, I didn't mean to drive into that median, I was just predicting the next token' apology.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI has updated its GPT-6 Astra model with the capability to operate a motor vehicle.

cooking.headline: Seattle bans dynamic grocery pricing so your milk doesn't cost more during a heatwave
cooking.summary: Seattle just outlawed the 'dynamic pricing' dream where stores charge you more for bread simply because you look stressed or it's raining outside. It's a huge win for shoppers who prefer their grocery bills to be as static as a legacy codebase.
cooking.plain_english: The Seattle City Council has passed a law that prohibits grocery stores from using surveillance data to change prices for individual customers in real time.

cooking.headline: The UK is officially 'it' in the world's most expensive game of tag
cooking.summary: The UK military is jamming satellites to protect its interests, effectively treating space like a noisy coffee shop with bad Wi-Fi. It turns out that when you can't fix your own connection, the best defense is making sure nobody else has one either.
cooking.plain_english: The United Kingdom is using signal jamming technology to disrupt foreign satellites as a defensive measure.

cooking.headline: The open-source AI landscape is changing faster than a framework update
cooking.summary: The balance of power in open-source AI models is shifting so quickly that being the industry leader has the shelf life of a carton of milk. It's hard to build a long-term strategy when your foundational model becomes legacy code by next Tuesday.
cooking.plain_english: The competitive landscape for open-source artificial intelligence models is evolving rapidly with frequent changes in leadership.

cooking.headline: The cost of intelligence is crashing, yet my code still has the same bugs.
cooking.summary: Intelligence is becoming a cheap commodity while the price of human patience remains at an all-time high. It turns out that having a genius-level AI doesn't actually solve the problem of me forgetting a semicolon.
cooking.plain_english: The cost of running advanced artificial intelligence models is decreasing significantly over time.

cooked.headline: The Pentagon just proved that 'move fast and break things' is a terrible strategy for missiles
cooked.summary: The military is blaming an overreliance on AI for a strike on a school, essentially turning a war zone into a debugging session gone wrong. It turns out that when you push to production without a human in the loop, the edge cases involve real-world casualties.
cooked.plain_english: The United States Department of Defense reported that an excessive dependence on artificial intelligence led to a missile strike on a school in Iran.

cooked.headline: Australia wants an algorithm opt-out button, and the US is calling it censorship
cooked.summary: Australia is trying to force platforms to let users opt out of algorithmic feeds, but the US thinks that's a polite way of saying 'break the engagement loop.' It's the digital equivalent of a parent trying to turn off the TV while the kid is mid. binge.
cooked.plain_english: The United States government is criticizing proposed Australian legislation that would require social media platforms to allow users to disable personalized algorithm-based feeds.

cooked.headline: Radicle's decentralized code sharing just hit a centralized snag
cooked.summary: Radicle promised a future where your code is safe from single points of failure, but a protocol vulnerability just reminded us that even decentralized networks have bugs. Nothing humbles a peer-to-peer enthusiast quite like a patch note.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability was discovered in the Radicle network protocol that allows for unauthorized actions.

cooked.headline: Samsung just turned your fridge into an expensive paperweight
cooked.summary: Samsung pushed a software update that managed to brick their smart fridges, effectively turning your kitchen appliance into a frozen hunk of metal. It's the ultimate 'it works on my machine' moment, provided your machine isn't supposed to keep your milk from spoiling.
cooked.plain_english: A software update from Samsung caused their smart refrigerators to stop functioning properly.

cooked.headline: 28% of job listings are ghost jobs, the ultimate 'we'll get back to you' move.
cooked.summary: Companies are keeping nearly a third of their job postings active for months just to maintain the aesthetic of growth. It's the corporate equivalent of leaving a 'Help Wanted' sign in the window of a shop that closed three years ago.
cooked.plain_english: A large portion of job advertisements on company websites remain active for more than three months without actually leading to new hires.
